alalal-c44099-d1e104.summary: Rubric of Article 5: whether God is rightly said to be in things in five modes.

alalal-c44099-d1e113.summary: Introduces questions on Lombard's text, beginning with his claim that God is in every nature presentially, potentially and essentially.

alalal-c44099-d1e127.summary: First objection: the modes are taken either from God, who relates in one way to all, so there are not five; or from creatures, in which God works differently, so there would be infinitely many, not five.

alalal-c44099-d1e161.summary: Second objection: 'God is in us by grace' either adds something on God's side, making him variable, which is heretical, or adds only a connoted effect in us, so that on God's side it is the same as presence by essence and not a special mode.

alalal-c44099-d1e185.summary: Third objection: the effect relates to the cause as the cause to the effect; since things are in God in only one way, God should be in things in one way, not five.

alalal-c44099-d1e198.summary: Fourth objection: if the three modes mean the thing's essence is from God's essence and its power from his power, the third fails, since a thing's presence cannot be from its own presence; not everything is present to itself, since that implies self-knowledge.

alalal-c44099-d1e224.summary: Further: if we abstract from a thing's power and presence, they would no longer come from God's power and presence, yet God would still be in the thing's essence in all three ways, so that explanation fails.

alalal-c44099-d1e242.summary: Fifth objection: if the modes follow the attributes of the persons, 'essentially' cannot be appropriated to any person, and if power is the Father's and presence the Son's through knowledge, nothing is left for the Holy Spirit.

alalal-c44099-d1e264.summary: Further: even abstracting from the persons, God would still be in all things essentially, presentially and potentially.

alalal-c44099-d1e274.summary: Further: Father, Son and Holy Spirit are each in all things in all three ways, so the modes belong to them not as distinguished by properties or appropriations but as sharing the divine essence.

alalal-c44099-d1e296.summary: Solution, without prejudice: the modes can be distinguished in three ways. First, by the connoted effect, as exemplar flows into exemplified: the thing's essence from God's essence, its species from his presence through the idea in the divine mind, its power from his power. Second, by five items in God: the essence considered without the persons, giving presence essentially; the Father's appropriated power, giving presence by power; the Son's wisdom, giving presence presentially; the Spirit's goodness, giving presence in the saints by indwelling grace; and the essence in a person, giving presence in the man Christ by union, since the essence is incarnate in the person.
claims: The five modes of divine presence can be correlated with the essence, the appropriated attributes of the three persons, and the essence as incarnate in a person.

alalal-c44099-d1e359.summary: Answers the objection that without the persons God would still be in things in the three ways: even if the persons are not understood, their attributes remain, and the essence, preceding power, together with wisdom, power and goodness, would still create creatures and give grace to rational ones, so the account stands.

alalal-c44099-d1e385.summary: A subtler and more relevant account: the simpler a thing, the wider its extent, so the supremely simple encompasses all and God's essential presence is caused by simplicity, as Augustine says. Presence comes from penetrating subtlety, for nothing is subtler than the simplest, and Hebrews 4:12-13 says the word of God penetrates all and everything lies open before him. Presence by power comes from the first cause's influence on all power, since nothing moves unless the first moves. Under God two things act, nature and free choice: to nature God is present in the three ways, reduced to simplicity, subtlety and the ratio of moving; to free choice he is present as raising it above nature, which happens only by grace, hence by indwelling grace, presupposing the three modes. His presence in the man Christ is special and miraculous.
claims: Essential presence follows from divine simplicity, presential presence from penetrating subtlety, and potential presence from the first cause's universal influence.
Presence by grace is God's elevating free choice above nature and presupposes the three natural modes.
God's presence in Christ is a special, miraculous mode.

alalal-c44099-d1e485.summary: Reply to the first objection: the modes are taken from both God and creatures. God relates to all things without variation in his essence or anything added to him, but not according to the same aspect of exemplar for every thing.
claims: God relates invariably to all things in essence but under different aspects of exemplarity.

alalal-c44099-d1e516.summary: Reply to the second objection: indwelling by grace connotes a different effect that raises nature further, and a different aspect of the exemplar, that of good will. The Spirit is given with his gifts, not as another than before, but for another purpose, if indeed he was possessed before, which he was not by those in whom God is only by essence, presence and power. It adds no new reality, but a new mode of signifying, which suffices in divine things.
claims: Indwelling by grace adds a new connoted effect and mode of signifying, not a change in God.

alalal-c44099-d1e554.summary: Reply to the third objection: the relation of effect to cause is one with respect to inherence, but not conversely, since the cause does not need the effect, while the effect needs the cause in many ways; so the cause's presence in the effect is distinguished into several modes on account of the effect's need.
claims: The plurality of God's modes of presence reflects the creature's manifold dependence, not any need in God.

alalal-c44099-d1e578.summary: Reply to the fourth objection: Albert concedes that the explanation it attacked is less satisfactory.

alalal-c44099-d1e587.summary: Reply to the fifth objection: if the modes are taken from the persons' attributes, one should proceed as at the start of the solution, since only a forced exposition could reduce the essential mode to a particular person.

alalal-c44099-d1e605.summary: Concludes that this resolves all the objections.

alalal-c44099.summary: Article 5 examines Lombard's five modes of God's presence in things: by essence, presence and power in all things, by indwelling grace in the saints, and by union in Christ. The objections argue that a simple God relates to all in one way, that grace either changes God or adds nothing, and that the proposed correlations with attributes or persons fail. Albert offers three non-exclusive accounts. One follows the connoted effects of exemplarity. One matches the five modes to the essence, the appropriated attributes of Father (power), Son (wisdom) and Spirit (goodness), and the essence incarnate in a person. The preferred one derives essential presence from simplicity, presential presence from penetrating subtlety, and potential presence from the first cause's universal influence. These three apply to nature; grace adds God's elevating of free choice above nature, and union in Christ is special and miraculous. The plurality of modes reflects the creature's manifold dependence and different aspects of exemplarity, not any variation in God.
claims: God is in creatures in five modes: by essence, presence and power in all, by indwelling grace in the saints, and by union in Christ.
The three general modes derive from divine simplicity, subtlety and first causality.
Presence by grace elevates free choice above nature and adds a mode of signifying, not a change in God.
The diversity of modes reflects creaturely dependence, not divine variability.
